tasks.description: Create a data retention policy that deletes user activity data after 30 days for GDPR compliance. This policy should be enforced by an automated pipeline and apply to all user activity records without exception.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user activity record, when 30 days have passed since collection, then the record is deleted from the event store.

tasks.description: Design and implement a primary event store to hold user activity data. The store should be queryable by internal tools and restricted to authorized personnel.
acceptance_criteria: Given an event, when stored in the event store, then it can be queried by internal tools.

tasks.description: Restrict access to the event store to authorized personnel and log all access for auditing purposes.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unauthorized user, when attempting to access the event store, then access is denied and the attempt is logged.

tasks.description: Implement a data archiving mechanism to retain historical event logs indefinitely for trend analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Given a historical event log, when queried, then the log is returned and can be analyzed.

tasks.description: Create an automated job to delete user activity data older than 30 days from the event store.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user activity record older than 30 days, when the automated deletion job runs, then the record is deleted from the event store.

tasks.description: Log all access to the event store and user activity data for auditing purposes.
acceptance_criteria: Given an access attempt to the event store, when the attempt is made, then the attempt is logged for auditing purposes.

tasks.description: Reconcile the conflicting requirements between GDPR compliance and analytics stakeholders to ensure the data retention policy meets both needs.
acceptance_criteria: Given the data retention policy, when reviewed by stakeholders, then the policy meets both GDPR compliance and analytics requirements.
